parsed_answer.content: Artifact repositories, specifically enterprise-grade solutions like Nexus and Artifactory, serve as the definitive centralized single source of truth for all binary components, build outputs, and third-party dependencies in modern software engineering lifecycles. When building complex object-oriented systems or distributed architectures, teams rely heavily on external and internal libraries. Without a managed repository manager, projects suffer from fragmented dependency trees, broken transitive resolution, and severe supply-chain vulnerabilities. Nexus and Artifactory solve this by acting as intelligent proxy caches, local release registries, and snapshot stores. They implement strict containment policies, cryptographic checksum validation, and role-based access control, ensuring that every build pulls immutable, deterministic artifacts across local developer machines and automated CI/CD pipelines.

items: Proxy Repositories cache remote public registries (like Maven Central or npmjs) locally to dramatically accelerate build times and protect teams against upstream outages or deletion of upstream packages (left-pad scenario).

Virtual Repositories aggregate multiple local and remote repositories under a single unified URL endpoint, allowing developers and build agents to resolve internal and external dependencies seamlessly without changing configuration files.

Snapshot vs Release Management enforces strict lifecycle boundaries; Snapshots allow mutable, iterative integration builds, while Releases are flagged as immutable binaries to guarantee absolute deterministic reproducibility in production deployments.

parsed_answer.content: Production Gotcha: Never check static cleartext deployment passwords into your build scripts. Always inject repository credentials via environment variables or secret managers (like Vault). Furthermore, configure aggressive cleanup and retention policies for snapshot repositories, or your artifact storage volume will silently expand, exhausting cloud storage quotas and severely degrading database index performance inside the repository manager.
